symbols.name: B
symbols.def: \(B_j(a,z)\) is the lexicographically selected orthonormal basis of \(L_2^0(q_j)\) obtained by Gram--Schmidt

symbols.name: Cprof
symbols.def: \(C^{\mathrm{prof}}(g)=\operatorname{hull}\{s\in[-\rho,\rho]:D(s;g)\le c(s)\}\), with \(\{0\}\) for an empty inversion

symbols.name: NM
symbols.def: \(N_M\) is the exact number of CDF calls at level \(M\)

assumptions.condition: \(Y^\ell\mid X=j\sim N(\bar\mu_j,\sigma_j^2)\) under \(R_0\) for every \(\ell\in\{0,1\},j\in\mathcal J\)

novel.justification: A no-effect baseline is meaningful when proxies remain informative about a hidden exposure.
Designed diagnostic surrogates can be known to increase with latent disease status.

definitions.name: explicit local causal family
definitions.construction: For \(\eta\in\mathcal H_0(P_0)\) and \(t\in[-\rho,\rho]^J\), \(R_{n,\eta,t}\) has \(X\sim w\), \(L\mid X=j\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_j)\), conditionally independent \(A\mid L=\ell,X=j\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(a_{\ell j})\) and \(Z\mid L=\ell,X=j\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(b_{\ell j})\), and \(Y^0,Y^1\) independent of \(L,A,Z\) given \(X\), with independent coordinates \(Y^\ell\mid X=j\sim N(\bar\mu_j+(\ell-\pi_j)t_j/\sqrt n,\sigma_j^2)\). Set \(Y=Y^L\) and \(P_{n,\eta,t}=\operatorname{obs}_{\#}R_{n,\eta,t}\)

definitions.name: connected primal and two-measure dual
definitions.construction: The primal is \(V(\rho)\). Its dual is \(\sup_{\Lambda,\Gamma}\{(1-\alpha)\Gamma(\Theta_\rho)+\int\min_{(l,u)\in\mathcal A_\rho}\mathfrak G_{\Lambda,\Gamma}(g;l,u)\,d g\}\), with \(\Lambda\in\mathcal P(\Theta_\rho)\) and \(\Gamma\in\mathcal M_+(\Theta_\rho)\)

definitions.name: outward-rounded normal-CDF algorithm
definitions.construction: Allocate \(e_M=2^{-M}/N_M\) per call. Use \(\Phi(x)=\tfrac12[1+\operatorname{erf}(x/\sqrt2)]\), symmetry to reduce to \(x\in[0,T_M]\), and the fixed dyadic subdivision \(r_M=\lceil\log_2(2T_M)\rceil\), \(h_M=T_M/2^{r_M}\le1/2\). On each subinterval centered at \(c\), integrate the order-\(K_M\) Taylor polynomial of \(e^{-u^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\), with Hermite coefficients \(H_{k+1}(c)=cH_k(c)-kH_{k-1}(c)\), using outward rational intervals. Let \(D_{K+1}(T_M)=\max_{|u|\le T_M}|H_{K+1}(u)|e^{-u^2/2}\); choose the least \(K_M\) satisfying \[\frac{2^{r_M}D_{K_M+1}(T_M)h_M^{K_M+2}}{2^{K_M+1}(K_M+2)!\sqrt{2\pi}}\le\frac{2^{-M}}{N_M}.\] Directed rational enclosures of \(\pi,\sqrt2\), exponential values, and Hermite extrema yield \(\Phi_M(x)\)

definitions.name: finite CDF CAD certificate
definitions.construction: Use exact CAD for \(\eta,t\), mesh \(2^{-M}\), rational observation boxes in \([-M,M]^{3J}\), the full interval outside, and independent outward endpoint dither of width \(h=2^{-M}\). At fixed input, each box \(\prod_r[l_r,u_r]\) has probability enclosed solely by \(\prod_r[\Phi_M(u_r-m_r^G)-\Phi_M(l_r-m_r^G)]\). On each CAD cell \(C\), interval differentiation certifies \(L_C^m\ge\sup_C\|Dm^G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) and \(L_C^\psi\ge\sup_C\|D\psi^G\|_2\). Combine \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(N(m,I),N(m',I))\le\|m-m'\|_2/2\) with dither inclusion modulus \(2|\psi-\psi'|/h\): subtract \(C_{M,C}\operatorname{diam}(C)\) from coverage and dual lower bounds and add it to risk and primal upper bounds, reversing signs when the optimized inequality reverses. Define \(L_M\) and \(U_M\) solely from these finite CDF enclosures, Gaussian-tail enclosures, dither terms, and displayed moduli

definitions.name: curved-fiber solution handle
definitions.construction: Use the exact two-parameter chart at \(q^{\mathrm{curv}}\), quotient cell-exchange and sign symmetries, derive endpoint likelihood-ratio equations for the two-measure saddle, and isolate support changes with the finite CDF CAD certificates

statements.statement: For every legal \(\eta,t\), \(R_{n,\eta,t}\) satisfies consistency, exchangeability, proxy exclusion, and proxy conditional independence; its coordinates are \(\pi,a,b,\mu_n\), with \(\delta_{n,j}=\mu_{n,1j}-\mu_{n,0j}=t_j/\sqrt n\) and \(\sqrt n\,\theta_{n,\eta,t}=\sum_jw_jt_j=\psi^G(\eta,t)\). Under the observed pushforward, \(P_{n,\eta,t}(X=j)=w_j\), \(P_{n,\eta,t}(A=a,Z=z\mid X=j)=q_{j,az}\), and \(E_{P_{n,\eta,t}}[Y\mid A=a,Z=z,X=j]=\bar\mu_j+n^{-1/2}t_jk_{\eta,j}(a,z)\). Moreover \(P_{n,\eta,0}=P_0\)
statements.justification: This identifies the local coordinate as a genuine potential-outcome effect and derives its observed representation.
statements.gap: ZhouTchetgenTchetgen2024Hidden treats off-null identification; this result constructs the causal-null local score.
statements.consumer: It gives causal meaning to every Gaussian benchmark state.

statements.statement: The baseline law lies in \(\mathcal E_0(P_0)\), and \(\mathcal H_0(P_0)\) is exactly the compact semialgebraic set obeying the declared inequalities and \(q_{j,rs}=\sum_{\ell=0}^1\pi_j^\ell(1-\pi_j)^{1-\ell}a_{\ell j}^r(1-a_{\ell j})^{1-r}b_{\ell j}^s(1-b_{\ell j})^{1-s}\). Every point is attained by a full-data baseline law with pushforward \(P_0\)
statements.justification: Exact realizability prevents algebraic but causally illegal states.
statements.gap: ZwiernikSmith2011Inequalities shows why equality-only latent images are insufficient; this gives the maintained full-data image.
statements.consumer: It licenses finite CAD optimization without losing causal semantics.

statements.statement: Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal H_0(P_0)\) and \(t\in[-\rho,\rho]^J\). For iid \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\sim P_0\), the observed mixture likelihood has score \(\dot\ell_{\eta,j}(O)\) at \(t=0\) and \[\log\frac{dP_{n,\eta,t}^{\otimes n}}{dP_0^{\otimes n}}=m^G(\eta,t)^{\mathsf T}\Delta_n-\tfrac12\|m^G(\eta,t)\|_2^2+o_{P_0}(1).\] Under \(P_0^{\otimes n}\), \(\Delta_n\Rightarrow N(0,I_{3J})\); under \(P_{n,\eta,t}^{\otimes n}\), \(\Delta_n\Rightarrow N(m^G(\eta,t),I_{3J})\)
statements.justification: The result derives the Gaussian mean and identity covariance from the explicit causal mixture.
statements.gap: Classical LAN does not supply this posterior-contrast loading or its causal target equality.
statements.consumer: It establishes the fixed-input local benchmark without a uniform risk-transfer claim.

statements.statement: For \(J=1,\epsilon=1/10,q=q^{\mathrm{curv}},\sigma_1=1\), the legal fiber contains \(\eta_1=(1/2,1/5,4/5,3/10,7/10)\), \(\eta_2=(1/2,3/10,7/10,1/5,4/5)\), and \(\eta_3=(1/2,1/10,9/10,7/20,13/20)\), with posterior contrasts \(k_1=(-25/62,-5/38,5/38,25/62)\), \(k_2=(-25/62,5/38,-5/38,25/62)\), and \(k_3=(-55/124,-25/76,25/76,55/124)\). Since \(-(9/5)k_1+(7/10)k_2+k_3=0\) but the same coefficients sum to \(-1/10\), no common linear influence coordinate represents \(\psi^G\) over the fiber
statements.justification: The witness proves that legal nuisance ambiguity changes the score direction.
statements.gap: Kaji2021WeakIdentification is generic; this is a finite hidden-treatment incompatibility certificate.
statements.consumer: It rules out a single centered Gaussian influence interval on the curved benchmark.

statements.statement: For every fixed input and \(\rho>0\), the connected primal attains \(V(\rho)\), the two-measure dual attains with no gap, and an optimal kernel is supported almost everywhere on minimizers of \(\mathfrak G_{\Lambda^\star,\Gamma^\star}\). The measure \(\Lambda^\star\) is supported on worst-risk states and \(\Gamma^\star\) on binding-coverage states; these conditions are sufficient for optimality
statements.justification: The saddle gives the sharp connected-interval local benchmark and an attaining rule.
statements.gap: EvansHansenStark2005Minimax does not establish an endpoint-kernel saddle on a curved nuisance-indexed mean surface.
statements.consumer: It is the reference value for evaluating profile intervals.

statements.statement: For every fixed exact input, each certificate level terminates with \(0\le L_M\le V(\rho)\le U_M\le2\rho\), \(L_M\uparrow V(\rho)\), and \(U_M\downarrow V(\rho)\). Every observation-box probability is a finite product of one-dimensional \(\Phi_M\)-difference enclosures, and every CAD cell uses the explicit corrections \(\pm C_{M,C}\operatorname{diam}(C)\). Thus the first \(M\) with \(U_M-L_M\le\operatorname{tol}\) is found finitely, and weak-star limits of validated primal kernels attain \(V(\rho)\)
statements.justification: Finite CDF enclosures and explicit mesh moduli certify the continuum value from both sides.
statements.gap: SchaferStark2009Optimal and SchlemperMoreira2026ConfidenceSets do not provide these monotone connected-rule certificates.
statements.consumer: It produces auditable curved-fiber optimality and coverage brackets.

statements.statement: The calibrated profile hull is Borel, honest over \(\Theta_\rho\), and has regret \(\mathcal R^{\mathrm{prof}}(\rho)\). Its regret is zero if and only if some optimal dual pair makes its endpoints minimize \(\mathfrak G_{\Lambda^\star,\Gamma^\star}\) almost everywhere and satisfies both saddle support conditions; otherwise regret is strictly positive
statements.justification: This separates profile validity from local benchmark optimality.
statements.gap: EvansHansenStark2005Minimax does not analyze this profile hull on a hidden-treatment fiber.
statements.consumer: It determines when profiling can be retained without expected-length loss.

statements.statement: For \(J=1,\epsilon=1/10,q=q^{\mathrm{face}},\sigma_1=1\), the legal mechanism fiber is \(\{\eta_0\}\), the posterior contrast is \((-20/41,0,0,20/41)\), and the sufficient observation is \(X_G\sim N(\kappa t,1)\). If \(0<\kappa\rho\le2z_{1-\alpha}\), then \(V(\rho)\) equals the Evans--Hansen--Stark truncated-Pratt value divided by \(\kappa\), while \(\mathcal R^{\mathrm{prof}}(\rho)>0\); \(\alpha=0.05,\rho=1\) is legal
statements.justification: The active face recovers the published scalar optimum and yields legal strict profile regret.
statements.gap: The new content beyond EvansHansenStark2005Minimax is the exact hidden-treatment embedding and profile comparison.
statements.consumer: It gives a transparent regime where honest profiling is suboptimal.

statements.statement: At \(J=1,\epsilon=1/10,q=q^{\mathrm{curv}},\sigma_1=1\), what are the exact least-favorable support, \(V(\rho)\), and profile-regret phase transitions for all \(\rho>0\)? Can the symmetry-reduced endpoint equations and finite CDF CAD certificates give exact algebraic transition points and an attaining connected kernel on each radius cell?
statements.justification: The curved fiber is the first genuinely nuisance-direction-dependent benchmark.
statements.gap: Neither EvansHansenStark2005Minimax nor SchaferStark2009Optimal gives this phase diagram.
statements.consumer: The solution would provide a deployable null-effect interval benchmark for ambiguous proxy mechanisms.

sampling_model.design: The explicit iid full-data family \(R_{n,\eta,t}\) induces \(P_{n,\eta,t}\); its pointwise LAN limit is the Gaussian benchmark.
sampling_model.treatment: The causal treatment \(L\) is hidden and \(Y=Y(L)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The baseline full-data fiber obeys the declared compactness conditions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; no sampled-data rule or uniform risk transfer is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Off-null proxy relevance identifies hidden-treatment causal effects and supports semiparametric inference.
The truncated-Pratt procedure is minimax for a bounded normal mean when \(\tau\le2z_{1-\alpha}\).
Monte Carlo confidence regions converge over finite prior polytopes.
Structured inversion methods avoid component loss and control coverage error.
Tree cumulants describe binary latent-tree geometry and singular fibers.
Weakly regular parameters are nonlinear maps of regular reduced forms.

tldr: An explicit full-data causal family perturbs a legal null baseline by \(E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=j]=t_j/\sqrt n\), yields the observed posterior-contrast score, and has a fixed-input Gaussian LAN benchmark with target \(\sqrt n\,\theta=\sum_jw_jt_j\). The project solves the benchmark's connected-interval saddle, certifies it using only finite outward normal-CDF enclosures and explicit CAD-cell moduli, characterizes profile regret, and recovers bounded normal location on a legal active face. The curved-fiber phase diagram remains open.

project_justification.gap: Off-null hidden-treatment efficiency and existing minimax confidence-set theory do not solve connected decisions on the causal-null posterior-contrast fiber.
project_justification.niche: The explicit local family preserves causal meaning and produces a compact curved Gaussian state surface.
project_justification.fill: The fixed-input LAN theorem, connected saddle, finite CDF certificate, and exact profile-regret criterion fill this gap without asserting sampled-data risk transfer.

related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen provide the off-null causal framework and ADNI motivation, but only inform the present null construction. Zwiernik and Smith supply tripod geometry and legal-image inequalities. Kaji provides generic weak-regularity theory. Evans, Hansen, and Stark give the closest decision result and the bounded-normal optimum recovered here. Schafer and Stark approximate minimax regions over prior polytopes, while Schlemper and Moreira develop reliable structured inversion. None combines the explicit causal local mixture, curved connected saddle, finite outward-CDF certification, and profile-regret frontier.
technical_internal_limitation: The LAN claim is pointwise in fixed \(\eta,t\). There is no uniform equivalence over moving fibers or active cones, no sampled-data confidence rule or risk transfer, no nuisance estimator, no ADNI reanalysis, and no centered-efficiency claim.
honest_scope: The causal representation, legal projection, fixed-input LAN, curved witness, connected saddle, finite certificate, profile criterion, and bounded-normal embedding are to prove. The curved phase diagram is open. The bounded-normal face is the required known-result reduction. Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen remains an off-null comparator and future bridge only.

seed_details.reason: The preserved kernel is tied to an explicit causal local family by fixed-input LAN.
Finite outward CDF products and CAD moduli replace numerical integration.

literature_map: Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen anchors the off-null causal model; Zwiernik--Smith anchors legal tripod geometry; Evans--Hansen--Stark anchors minimax expected length and bounded normal location; Schafer--Stark and Schlemper--Moreira anchor computation and inversion; Kaji anchors generic weak regularity. The joint curved connected-saddle and finite two-sided certificate are not supplied by these sources.
